title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Risk-on week built on AMZN blowout; semis bled, software/China caught bids. Mega-cap earnings set the tone: a blowout AMZN report and a sharp AAPL miss drove flows from hardware into internet, software, and consumer names. Large caps outpaced small caps, energy fell, and volatility stayed compressed.

INDICES — SPY +1.10%, DIA +1.07%, QQQ +0.55%, IWM +0.01%. Large beat small by 0.69pp. VIX ended at 16.0, below its 20-day average of 17.2, for a lower-vol week. The most notable cross-asset move was oil's weekly reversal, USO -5.50% despite Friday's +1.33% bounce. No index in the data is flagged below its 200-day MA.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLY Consumer Discretionary +6.11%, XLC Communication Services +1.83%, XLF Financials +1.12%, XLP Staples +1.09%, XLV Health Care -0.01%, XLE Energy -0.12%, XLK Technology -0.30%, XLI Industrials -1.54%, XLB Materials -1.62%, XLRE Real Estate -1.92%, XLU Utilities -4.19%. Top Industries: KWEB +8.37%, IGV +7.50%. Bottom Industries: USO -5.50%, UTES -5.44%. Money rotated into consumer internet, China, and software, while utilities, energy, and semis saw selling. Rotation label: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — The tape was earnings-driven: AMZN's blowout report produced a 3.2x volume spike, AAPL's negative reaction came on 2.7x volume, and ETN jumped 7.32% on record quarterly sales. XLY led the sectors while SOXX fell -4.20% and XLU -4.19%, confirming money exited high-multiple hardware and defensives into software/consumer. VXN at 26.0 sat below its 20-day average of 27.5, and SPY ATM IV of 9.2% with skew +8.9% shows calm equity-derivative positioning. No macro catalyst is needed to explain the move; it was sector rotation and stock-specific earnings.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch whether SOXX can stabilize after its -10.85% 20-day drawdown against a +60.95% YTD trend; a bounce would confirm broad participation, further weakness would deepen the AI-hardware unwind. The XLY surge needs follow-through to keep the high-to-low rotation alive. Positioning ahead of the Sep 16 FOMC matters — hike odds sit at 65.9%, so any shift in rate expectations will hit the stretched consumer and software longs first.
